records.text:
My honest take on @arc Studio, as someone building DApps with Claude Code 🧵

I'm building PikaStake on Arc. You stake USDC, earn pUSDC, then burn it to mint Pokémon cards. There's also mystery boxes, .arc domains, and a section to mint your own NFT. 6 contracts, one index.html. I wrote almost all of it with Claude Code.

Let me be honest first: without Claude Code, this project wouldn't exist. But I kept getting stuck in the same places.

🧱 Where I struggled

• The contract side was messy. Getting the code written was easy. But compiling, deploying, verifying, then updating the new address in both index.html and .env were all separate steps, and I had to track every one of them myself.
• Arc has its own quirks. Gas is paid in USDC. Native USDC has 18 decimals, the ERC-20 interface uses 6. A general-purpose AI doesn't always know this, so I kept explaining it over and over.
• I learned security the hard way. We used unlimited (MaxUint256) approvals for box mints. Turns out wallet security engines like Blockaid flag that as a drainer pattern. We switched to exact-amount approvals. Nobody warned me beforehand.
• There was no real audit step. If it worked, it was "done."

🤖 So what is Arc Studio?

An AI agent from Circle. You describe what you want, and it writes the contract, tests it, audits it and deploys it to Arc testnet. It can build a frontend on top too. USDC, CCTP, Circle wallets, Gateway and x402 come preloaded.

The part that really matters: you don't have to use it only from the browser. It has a CLI and plugs into Claude Code as a subagent. You're not leaving Claude Code behind, you're adding an onchain specialist to the team.

🛠️ The model that clicked for me: two builders, one project

• Claude Code is the foreman. It runs on my machine, inside my repo, and knows how everything fits together.
• Arc Studio is the onchain specialist. It works in its own sandbox on Circle's servers. It has no access to my files and doesn't try to touch them.

Working between them feels like dropping a part off at a repair shop:

→ Claude Code sends the contract
→ Studio writes, tests, audits, deploys (a deploy can take 5–20 min)
→ One JSON comes back: what changed, the address, the tx hash, an explorer link
→ Claude Code pulls the files into my repo, and if I've edited a file by hand, it skips it instead of overwriting
→ Claude Code wires the new address into the frontend

✅ Where I'd use it first in PikaStake

• A full audit of all 6 contracts with the "max preset." I'd much rather have learned about the approval issue this way. Another example: right now in PikaBoxes, the browser picks which card you get and keeps it in local storage. So the card doesn't actually exist onchain. A good audit would catch that right away.
• New contracts, like an ERC-721 that actually puts box cards onchain. Studio writes, tests and deploys it, and Claude Code hooks it up to the frontend.
• Circle integrations, like bringing USDC over from another chain with CCTP and staking it. Studio already knows this stuff, so I don't have to paste docs into Claude every time.

❌ Where I wouldn't

• Frontend work. Claude Code is already right there and knows my repo. Sending that to Studio is just an extra round trip.
• Mainnet. Studio doesn't sign, fund or send mainnet transactions. I don't see that as a limitation, I see it as a seatbelt. The final signature comes from my own wallet.
• Anything sensitive. The CLI already refuses .env files, private keys and certs. Still, make it a habit to never even try.

💡 Good to know

• Studio's workspace is Foundry-based, my project is Hardhat. Solidity is Solidity, but the tests and scripts come back in Foundry format.
• Don't take what Studio says at face value. Check returned addresses on the explorer yourself.
• There's a daily usage quota. "arc-studio usage" shows how much you've used.
• Prompts are capped at 10,000 characters, so you send code as files instead of pasting it.

In short: building DApps with Claude Code already worked. But the contract side always had a gap: "Is it correct? Is it safe? Who's keeping track of the deploy?"

Arc Studio fills exactly that gap. It doesn't replace Claude Code, it adds an onchain specialist next to it.

The foreman stays on my machine, the specialist works in its own workshop, and I'm the one who signs at the end.

records.text:
A simulator can recreate a place, but it can’t tell you what changed there this morning.

That’s one of the reasons I keep looking into @vangrid_io

AI has access to an incredible amount of digital information already. The harder problem comes when machines have to understand places that are constantly changing in the real world.

A warehouse gets rearranged. A loading area changes. A new obstacle appears. A route looks different from the last time it was mapped.

Old data can only tell you how things used to look.

Vangrid is taking an interesting approach by letting someone on the ground capture those environments with a phone when fresh data is needed. The data then goes through privacy processing, verification and onchain recording before becoming usable spatial information.

That creates a much closer connection between what is happening in the physical world and what AI systems actually need to know.

For Physical AI, having a realistic simulation is useful.

NVIDIA が出資する AI クラウドの Lambda が、IPO 前の最終ラウンドで最大 40 億ドル（約 6,400 億円）を調達中だ。評価額は 145 億ドル（約 2.3 兆円）と報じられた。

📊 調達額：最大 40 億ドル
📊 評価額：145 億ドル（プレマネー、調達前の値札）

Lambda は GPU クラウド、つまり NVIDIA のチップを貸し出す「AI の電力会社」。OpenAI や Anthropic のようなモデル開発企業が、自前で GPU を買わずに計算資源を借りる先だ。

① NVIDIA がバックにつく企業がこれだけの額を集められる = AI インフラ投資はまだ減速していない
② IPO 前の値札が 145 億ドルなら、上場後の初値はその上を試す公算

Marvell上調2031財年營收目標至最高900億美元

Marvell預估2031財年營收700億至900億美元，遠高於市場原估約438億美元；但股價今年已漲近250%、預估本益比約50倍，目標能否達成仍有賴AI資料中心需求長期兌現。

成長主軸有兩項。Marvell預計客製化晶片業務在2031財年貢獻300億美元，現有客戶包括Alphabet與Amazon等大型AI雲端業者；資料中心互連業務則估達375億美元，涵蓋資料中心內部及跨資料中心的資料傳輸網路連接方案。

公司也把2028年營收目標，從8月提出的180億美元上調至約200億美元，高於LSEG彙整分析師平均預期的182億美元。執行長Matt Murphy公布目標後，股價盤中一度漲7.2%至290.82美元。

這份展望反映的不是單靠單一AI晶片，而是客製化運算與高速互連能否同步擴張。若雲端業者持續加大AI資料中心建置，互連可能成為與ASIC同等關鍵的營收支柱；反之，市場已給出的高成長期待，也會提高目標執行的壓力。

Marine Le Pen unveiled a much more aggressive plan to cut government spending, seeking to reassure bond markets as France faces growing fiscal pressure.

Strong mega-cap earnings and AI expectations

The potential deal reflects intensifying competition for critical HDD components as AI data-center storage demand continues to rise.

NextEra Energy’s proposed $67B acquisition of Dominion Energy is facing political opposition in Virginia.

Critics are raising concerns over electricity costs, jobs and the regulatory implications of combining two major utilities.

The deal could become an important test of U.S. utility consolidation amid the broader push to expand power infrastructure.

🎬 $PSKY

The investment gives Shinsegae exposure to major global entertainment IP, including Paramount and Warner Bros. franchises, while supporting its broader strategy to connect content with retail, theme parks and future entertainment businesses.

🏥 $BDX

05 · MARKET FOCUS

Today’s market is being pulled in opposite directions.

On one side, AI earnings expectations, mega-cap strength and massive data-center investment continue to support equities.

On the other, long-term Treasury yields remain at multi-decade highs, market breadth is narrowing and higher financing costs are beginning to affect corporate investment decisions.

Meanwhile, falling oil prices could provide some relief by easing near-term inflation pressure.

Watch three things today:

1️⃣ Treasury auction demand and long-term yields
2️⃣ Fed speakers and their reaction to inflation risks

$NOK 透露了一个很重要的 AI 基建信号：现在限制行业增长的，可能不是需求，而是“能不能更快地把设备造出来”。

诺基亚管理层一句话很值得注意：

“如果我们能够以 2 倍的速度建设，我们的客户就能够以 2 倍的速度建设——而且他们很可能真的会这样做。”

这句话背后的含义非常直接：AI 基础设施的实际需求，可能仍然高于目前整个供应链能够交付的速度。

这也是为什么我一直认为，AI 下一阶段不能只盯着 $NVDA 的 GPU。

GPU 只是第一层。

当越来越多电力被接入新的数据中心园区，更多 GPU 集群真正开始上线之后，下一个必须同步扩张的，就是数据中心之间、园区之间，以及 GPU 集群内部的高速网络与光通信。

而这正是 $NOK 收购 Infinera 后值得重新关注的地方。

Infinera 带来的核心并不是普通电信设备，而是高速光传输能力。AI 集群规模越大，数据需要移动的距离越远，网络带宽和光学设备的重要性就越高。

过去一个 AI 数据中心可能只是一个园区。

未来可能变成：

一个园区 → 多个园区
一个区域 → 多个区域
单一 GPU 集群 → 超大规模分布式 AI 集群

这时候真正的问题已经不只是“有没有 GPU”，而是：

GPU 之间能不能足够快地交换数据？

不同数据中心之间能不能高速互联？

新的电力接入之后，网络设备能不能同步交付？

所以 AI 资本开支的资金流正在越来越清楚：

$NVDA / $AVGO —— 计算

$MU / $SKHY —— HBM 与内存

$ANET / $MRVL —— 高速网络

$LITE / $COHR / $AAOI —— 光模块与光器件

$CIEN / $NOK —— 光传输与数据中心互联

$VRT —— 电力与冷却

$VST / $CEG / $BE —— 电力供应

这其实是一条连续的产业链。

芯片解决“算力有没有”。

电力解决“GPU 能不能开机”。

而光网络解决的是——这些算力能不能真正连接起来，形成一个巨大的 AI 计算系统。

更值得注意的是，如果诺基亚所说的情况属实——客户并不是不愿意建设，而是供应速度限制了他们建设——那么这意味着光通信需求很可能仍然处于供给追赶需求的阶段，而不是需求见顶阶段。

这也是为什么 AI 基建行情正在从最早期的 GPU，逐渐向网络、光通信、电力和数据中心基础设施扩散。

市场最容易犯的错误，就是等到收入已经全面爆发以后，才意识到下一轮资本开支到底流向哪里。

现在真正值得观察的问题已经变成：

如果 AI 数据中心建设速度再翻一倍，$NOK、$CIEN、$LITE、$COHR、$AAOI 这一整条光通信产业链，谁会拿走最大的一块增量？
